This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #25570: Requests support for multiple skills in a single prompt — directly covers the multi-skill combination use case

- #35341: Requests auto-registering each skill as its own `/` slash command (per-skill slash commands)

### Likely root cause: one global layer memo map shared across two runtimes

I dug into this further. The hang happens **while the app service graph is being built on the first request** (it never reaches the request handler, so no `creating instance` is logged), and it looks like a lock-ordering deadlock caused by **two different `ManagedRuntime`s building overlapping layers into the same shared memo table**.

The pieces (paths on `main`):

1. A single global memo map, shared by every runtime:
   - `packages/core/src/effect/memo-map.ts`
     ```ts
     export const memoMap = Layer.makeMemoMapUnsafe()
     ```
   - `packages/core/src/effect/runtime.ts` — every `makeRuntime` passes it:
     ```ts
     ManagedRuntime.make(Layer.provideMerge(layer, Observability.layer), { memoMap })
     ```

2. **Runtime A** — the whole app, built lazily on the first request:
   - `packages/opencode/src/effect/app-runtime.ts`
     ```ts
     const rt = ManagedRuntime.make(AppLayer, { memoMap })
     ```
     `AppLayer` includes `Npm.node`, `FSUtil.node`, `Provider.node`, `LSP.node`, etc.

3. **Runtime B** — a second standalone runtime over `Npm`, sharing the same memo map:
   - `packages/core/src/npm.ts`
     ```ts
     const { runPromise } = makeRuntime(Service, LayerNode.compile(node))
     export async function add(...)   { return runPromise(svc => svc.add(...)) }
     export async function which(...) { return runPromise(svc => svc.which(...)) }
     ```
     `Npm.node`'s deps (`FSUtil`, `Global`, `EffectFlock`) are all **also** inside `AppLayer`.

4. Those plain `Npm.add` / `Npm.which` functions are called from services that are part of `AppLayer` and run during graph construction — e.g. `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` (`await Npm.add(model.api.npm)`) and `packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts` (`await Npm.which(...)`).

### The deadlock

On the first request, runtime A starts building `AppLayer`. Mid-build, one of those layers calls a plain `Npm.*` function, which makes **runtime B** start building `Npm` + `FSUtil`/`Global`/`EffectFlock` into the **same** memo table that runtime A is concurrently building. Each memo entry is guarded by a build latch; if runtime A holds (say) `FSUtil`'s latch and waits on `EffectFlock`, while runtime B holds `EffectFlock`'s latch and waits on `FSUtil`, neither can finish. Both fibers park on a memo latch forever — which matches the observed state exactly: the process is idle (CPU 0%), no network, no child processes, blocked internally.

It only deadlocks when the two concurrent builds interleave in the unlucky order, which is why it is intermittent and much more likely on a single-CPU machine.

This is also consistent with everything I could rule out: it reproduces with all plugins disabled (`Provider`/`LSP` still build), there is no network or npm activity while hung (the stall is on the in-memory latch, before any real work), and it happens before any session/instance is created.

### Suggested fix

Don't share one global `makeMemoMapUnsafe()` across independently-triggered runtimes. Either:

- give each `makeRuntime` (and the standalone `Npm` runtime) its **own** memo map, so there is never a second concurrent builder of the same layer, or
- drop the standalone `Npm` runtime and expose `Npm` only as the Effect service already provided by `AppLayer`, so `Npm.add`/`which` run on the one app runtime instead of a second one.

Either removes the cross-runtime latch cycle. Just lowering the app-build concurrency would narrow the race window but not close it.

@ariane-emory Bash _does_ do `C-y` as yank by default. So does readline. Was your test with some customized shell environment?

https://www.gnu.org/savannah-checkouts/gnu/bash/manual/bash.html#Readline-Killing-Commands-1

> `C-k`
> Kill the text from the current cursor position to the end of the line.
> 
> `C-y`
> Yank the most recently killed text back into the buffer at the cursor.

https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/readline.3.html

Thanks for the duplicate check. I've reviewed both issues — this is related but distinct:

- **#32713** asks for periodic session-state snapshots (SQLite flush, JSON caches) and a UI restore dialog. The focus is on data persistence.
- **#35505** reports a bug where sessions never make it to the database before a crash.

This request is narrower: it tracks which sessions were active (a lightweight manifest of session IDs) and auto-resumes the most recently active session on next startup — no manual lookup, no --continue flag, no UI prompt. It complements #32713 (which could still add periodic DB flushing) and #35505 (which is a separate durability bug).

The $1.80 already includes the cache reads at the published rate. The 5-hour bar is that amount after Pro’s Usage factor.

DeepSeek V4 Pro is **Usage $15** in the table, so quota is `visible × (60 / 15) = 4×` against the shared $12 / $30 / $60 windows:

https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#usage-limits

50% of $12 is **$6**. $1.80 × 4 = **$7.20**. Local `stats --days 1` is a calendar day; the bar is a 5-hour window, so a little of that $1.80 is already outside it.

13.9M cache reads at $0.022/M = **$0.31**, which is already inside the $1.03 Pro line. At Pro input ($0.66/M) those same reads would be **$9.20**, and the rolling bar would already be past 75% from cache alone. It is at 50%. Cache is not being billed as input.

The compaction call never tells the model it is summarizing.

`PROMPT_COMPACTION` says “Do not continue the conversation” and is assigned to a hidden agent:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e2505d434a6d78904ecfe546c4a1980d26bd8cd1/packages/core/src/plugin/agent.ts#L33-L37

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e2505d434a6d78904ecfe546c4a1980d26bd8cd1/packages/core/src/plugin/agent.ts#L180-L185

The request does not load that agent. It sends one user message and `tools: []`:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e2505d434a6d78904ecfe546c4a1980d26bd8cd1/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L201-L209

The body is the serialized transcript (`[Assistant tool call]: …`, `[Assistant reasoning]: …`). A DeepSeek reasoning model continues that turn instead of filling the summary template, which is the captured output here.

#43247 is the send-site. Stripping reasoning from the serialized history would help this model; it would not supply the missing “summarize, do not continue” instruction.

The VPP text is the compaction template filled from model weights, because the compaction system prompt is never sent.

Since 1.18 the call is one user message (`buildPrompt` + the `## Next Move` template) and `tools: []`. `PROMPT_COMPACTION` is registered on a hidden agent and not attached:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e2505d434a6d78904ecfe546c4a1980d26bd8cd1/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L160-L174

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e2505d434a6d78904ecfe546c4a1980d26bd8cd1/packages/core/src/plugin/agent.ts#L33-L37

A local Qwen with no system prompt fills the empty slots. The second `/compact` is the same request, so it invents another summary. 1.17.20 still delivered a compaction instruction, which is why reverting fixed it.

Adding evidence for a case that may be broader than the detach/reattach framing here: on my machine the `question` form does not render **even when the TUI was attached the whole time**, so there is no missed live event to replay. If you consider that a separate bug I am happy to file it separately, but the root cause you describe (pending question state is transient and only announced once) fits what I see, so I would rather add data here first. Noting that #36603 is closed unmerged.

**Still reproducing on 1.18.18**, most recently today (2026-08-19).

**The server path is fine; only the TUI render is missing.** A `--pure` (no plugins) headless `opencode serve` drives the whole flow green: the tool blocks, `question.asked` publishes, `GET /question` lists the pending question, and `POST /question/{id}/reply {"answers":[["Alpha"]]}` completes the tool with the answer and emits `question.replied`. Everything the client needs is exposed and working.

**Not provider- or plugin-specific.** `github-copilot/gpt-5.5`, a native provider, fails identically: `Tool execution aborted`, `metadata.interrupted: true`, ~27s.

**The regression brackets to v1.14.24…v1.15.5.** From `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, `question` tool parts by day and status:

| period | completed | aborted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-03-31 … 2026-04-25 | 59 | a handful (normal dismissals) |
| 2026-05-18 … 2026-08-19 | 1 | every other one |

The single `completed` after that boundary is the headless `POST /question/{id}/reply` test above, i.e. not a TUI render. Every TUI-driven one since 2026-05-18 ends `Tool execution aborted` with `metadata.interrupted: true`, after 8s to 5300s depending on how long I waited before giving up. The only escape is interrupting.

Worth distinguishing from a healthy failure: `The user dismissed this question` means the form **did** render and the operator declined. That is not this. This is silence, then an abort.

Happy to run anything specific against a build if it helps.

## Additional reproduction: LiteLLM proxy 402 terminal_quota_exhausted

Reproduced the same silent-stop with a **LiteLLM proxy** returning `402 terminal_quota_exhausted` for quota-exhausted providers (Alibaba Token Plan, OpenCode Go, Z.AI).

### Environment

- opencode 1.18.18
- LiteLLM proxy v1.97.0 (Docker) with custom_callbacks.py that transforms quota-exhaustion 429s into 402 `terminal_quota_exhausted`
- oh-my-openagent 4.19.4 (npm latest) with runtime_fallback hook

### Live evidence

Session `ses_fea3bf10bffelWmR3Za9oHPf23` (Sisyphus ultraworker, 5.8M input tokens) spawned subagents on `glm-5.2` / `minimax-m3` during Token Plan weekly quota exhaustion (before 2026-08-19 19:53 UTC reset).

Event DB shows:
- `message.updated` with `role: assistant`, `modelID: glm-5.2` — **no error.name, no error.data**
- **Zero `message.part.updated` events with assistant text/tool content** follow
- Session lifetime: 684ms–2s (directly stale)
- No `MessageAbortedError` recorded (unlike the omo internal-abort path which DOES write it)

This matches the silent-clean-stop path: provider stream terminates mid-generation (quota exhausted → 402 → stream ends without finish reason/usage), opencode records `finish=unknown`, zero tokens, no text, exits the agent loop normally. Parent subagent gets empty result with no error signal.

### Key distinction: two separate stale mechanisms

1. **omo internal abort path** (MessageAbortedError IS written): omo's runtime_fallback hook aborts via `abortSessionRequest()`, opencode records `MessageAbortedError`. This is noisy but visible. Fix: oh-my-openagent PR #6764 (merged to dev 2026-08-18, not in 4.19.4 release).

2. **opencode silent-clean-stop path** (NO error written): provider stream ends without finish reason, opencode exits agent loop as normal completion. This is the path described in this issue (#37852) and #41469. **No omo-side fix can detect this** because opencode reports it as a clean stop, not an error.

### Impact

The silent-clean-stop is particularly dangerous for subagent workflows: the parent agent receives an empty task result with no error signal, cannot distinguish "provider dropped" from "agent finished with nothing to say," and may proceed as if the subagent completed successfully.

### Related

- #41469 (same symptom, different reporter)
- PR #40531 (proposed fix — retry empty unknown responses)
- oh-my-openagent #6959 (omo-side stale on 402 quota — fixed in dev via #6764)
- oh-my-openagent #6665 (delegate-task poll waits 30 min on empty finish=unknown)
